dedupe_keys.name: combining a daily temperature pattern analysis and a heat pulse system to estimate sediment depths in sewer systems

description: Manuel Regueiro-Picallo and colleagues at Universidade da Coruña describe MONTSE, which combines sediment thermal-property measurement with temperature-pattern modelling. A dual-probe heat-pulse system characterises material properties; a surrogate model relates damped water/sediment temperature patterns to deposit depth. Related source descriptions establish an earlier one-dimensional heat-transfer formulation and later flow-sensitivity and gully-pot applications. These are linked formulations and experiments, not interchangeable validation datasets. Laboratory results reported for the 2024 study include maximum depth errors below 22 mm and estimated uncertainty of±7.3 mm. Zenodo provides its article freely under CC BY 4.0; the earlier article has CC BY-NC 4.0 terms. Coverage is method-dependent and not validated globally; the linked physical model simulates heat transfer. Related experimental records preserve campaign identities. A limitation is that equations, source code and measured values were not read, and the publication licence does not license an uninspected implementation.
